See also: peluché

French

[edit]
French Wikipedia has an article on:
peluche
Wikipedia fr

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French peluchier (“to peel; pluck”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pə.lyʃ/
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

peluche f (plural peluches)

  1. plush (toy), fluff

Derived terms

[edit]
  • ours en peluche

Related terms

[edit]
  • pelucher

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Dutch: pluche
  • → English: plush
  • → German: Plüsch
    • → Czech: plyš
    • → Hungarian: plüss
    • → Kashubian: plisz
    • → Lower Sorbian: pliš
    • → Polish: plusz
    • → Silesian: plisz
    • → Upper Sorbian: plyš
  • → Italian: peluche
  • → Portuguese: peluche
  • → Russian: плюш (pljuš)
    • → Yiddish: פּליוש (plyush)
  • → Spanish: peluche
  • → Turkish: pelüş, peluş (misspelling)

Verb

[edit]

peluche

  1. inflection of pelucher:
    1. first/third-person singular present indicative/subjunctive
    2. second-person singular imperative

Further reading

[edit]
  • “peluche”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Anagrams

[edit]
  • épluche, épluché

Italian

[edit]
Italian Wikipedia has an article on:
peluche
Wikipedia it

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • peluscia
  • peluscio
  • pelusce

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French peluche.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

peluche m (invariable)

  1. soft toy, plush
  2. plush (fabric)

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
peluche
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French peluche, from Old French peluchier.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /peˈlu.ʃi/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /peˈlu.ʃi/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /peˈlu.ʃe/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /pɨˈlu.ʃɨ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /pɨˈlu.ʃɨ/
    • (Northern Portugal) IPA(key): /pɨˈlu.t͡ʃɨ/

  • Hyphenation: pe‧lu‧che

Noun

[edit]

peluche m (plural peluches)

  1. (Portugal) plush
    Um ursinho de peluche.
    A teddy bear.
  2. (Portugal) a plush toy
    Synonym: pelúcia
    Este peluche é bastante fofo.
    This plush toy is very soft.
  3. fluffiness, fluff

Further reading

[edit]
  • “peluche”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “peluche”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
peluche
Wikipedia es

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French peluche.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /peˈlut͡ʃe/ [peˈlu.t͡ʃe]
  • Rhymes: -utʃe
  • Syllabification: pe‧lu‧che

Noun

[edit]

peluche m (plural peluches)

  1. (textiles) plush
  2. (toys) soft toy, stuffed animal

Derived terms

[edit]
  • osito de peluche

Further reading

[edit]
  • “peluche”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
